passage: Consumer protection is essential for everyone, regardless of their education or economic status, because exploitation can happen to any buyer in any marketplace. Sellers may use unfair practices like adulteration or overcharging, even in high-end branded stores, so consumers must remain vigilant everywhere. To help buyers identify quality, the government mandates certification marks. For instance, the ISI mark is used for industrial and electrical goods, while the Agmark is specifically for agricultural products. These symbols act as a guarantee of quality and safety standards. If a consumer feels cheated, they do not need to approach the highest court in the land for every issue. Instead, the Consumer Protection Act (COPRA) established a three-tier quasi-judicial machinery. Consumers can file complaints at the District, State, or National level depending on the value of the goods or services and the compensation claimed. This system ensures that justice is accessible and affordable for all citizens, moving away from the idea that only the wealthy can seek legal redressal. By understanding these rights and the proper channels for grievances, every shopper can protect themselves from unfair trade practices effectively.

items.evidence: Sellers may use unfair practices like adulteration or overcharging, even in high-end branded stores, so consumers must remain vigilant everywhere.
items.q: Meena buys a costly item from a famous branded store. What should she keep in mind?
options: Even such a store may cheat, so she should check
Such a store is safe, so checking is a waste
Only small shops cheat, so she can relax
A complaint is needed only if she is poor
items.explain: Unfair practices can happen even in high-end branded stores, so every buyer must stay careful.

wrong.why: thinks branded shops cannot sell adulterated goods
thinks only poor people get exploited

items.evidence: For instance, the ISI mark is used for industrial and electrical goods, while the Agmark is specifically for agricultural products.
items.q: Which purchase would most likely carry the Agmark?
items.explain: Agmark is for agricultural products like wheat flour; ISI covers industrial and electrical goods.

wrong.why: thinks safety marks cover only food, not cooking gas items
thinks marks are for industrial goods only in the Agmark case

items.evidence: If a consumer feels cheated, they do not need to approach the highest court in the land for every issue.
items.q: Why do consumers not have to go to the Supreme Court for every complaint?
options: Lower consumer bodies can hear their complaints
Only the poor are allowed to go there
A lawyer is needed in every consumer court
Cases start at the National level if small
items.explain: COPRA set up a three-tier system, so complaints can be filed at District, State or National level.

wrong.why: thinks the Supreme Court is the only route, then mixes up who may use it
thinks a lawyer and heavy fee are compulsory
mixes up which level hears small claims

items.evidence: Consumers can file complaints at the District, State, or National level depending on the value of the goods or services and the compensation claimed.
items.q: How does a consumer decide where to file a complaint under COPRA?

By the education level of the consumer
By the brand name of the shop
By the lawyer the consumer has hired
items.explain: The level of filing depends on the value of the goods or services and the compensation claimed.

links the process to branded shops
